concerns.text: T003 assumes the existence of original videos in `data/videos/orig/` but no prior task produces these videos. This violates the producer‑before‑consumer rule and leaves a missing foundational data generation step.
T004 depends on the same original videos as T003, yet no earlier task creates them. The required data source is missing, breaking the data‑flow ordering.
T003 also requires a populated `data/patches/` directory for patch sampling, but no task in the list populates this directory. This is another missing producer dependency.

Task T004 is marked `[P]` (parallel‑safe) but writes `data/checksums/manifest.csv`, a file that is later appended to by T005. Concurrent execution would cause race conditions, so the `[P]` tag is unsafe.
Task T005 is also marked `[P]` yet it appends to the same `manifest.csv` written by T004 and updates `metadata.csv`. These shared writes are not parallel‑safe.
Task T007 is marked `[P]` but writes multiple checkpoint files and updates `results/training_log.csv`. Parallel runs could clash on the CSV, making the `[P]` designation inaccurate.
Task T008 is marked `[P]` yet it writes `results/per_seed.csv`, a file that must be uniquely written per seed. Parallel execution without coordination would lead to write conflicts.
Task T009 is marked `[P]` but writes `results/summary.csv`, which aggregates data from T008. Parallel runs could overwrite each other, so the `[P]` tag is unsafe.
Task T010 is marked `[P]` but generates figure files and a summary table that are also produced by T009/T011. Parallel execution could cause nondeterministic overwrites.
Task T011 is marked `[P]` yet writes `results/manual_inspection.csv`, a file that could be concurrently written if tasks are run in parallel, violating parallel safety.
Task T012 is marked `[P]` but records profiling results to `results/resource_profile.json`. If run in parallel with other tasks that also write to `results/`, file contention may occur.
Task T013 orchestrates the entire pipeline but is also marked `[P]`. As a driver script it must run sequentially; marking it parallel‑safe is misleading.

Task T014 depends on artifacts generated throughout the pipeline (figures, tables, etc.). It is correctly placed after all prior tasks, but the preceding missing producers (original videos, patches) mean its referenced artifacts may not exist, breaking the end‑to‑end independence of the user‑story group.

Task T015 re‑runs the workflow from scratch; it assumes all earlier tasks successfully produce their outputs. Because the pipeline lacks a task that generates the original videos and patches, this verification step cannot succeed, indicating an ordering gap.
